text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 1.9% today as oil prices spiked on geopolitical tension—Brent crude hit $113, its highest since May, after reports of planned U.S. strikes on Iran and the pullback of U.S. diplomats from Saudi Arabia. While higher crude prices typically benefit refiners, the sharp jump appears to have spooked the market; the stock has shed $17 over the past week despite refineries running at a healthy 93.4% capacity and gasoline inventories remaining relatively stable.

The broader concern may be that escalating Middle East conflict, while it supports crude values, threatens the stable supply chains refiners depend on. Added to that is competition creeping in from overseas—news this week about India's Reliance expanding its refining footprint and potentially taking more Venezuelan crude suggests the global refining market is shifting in ways that could pressure U.S. players long-term.
